messages:
miriam: heads-up — thinking about adding deferred checksum validation to the streaming weights loader. idea: validate signed manifest + header up front, but defer per-chunk sha256 until first page-read. tradeoffs?

praveen: interesting. big perf win for cold startup but what about silent corruption slipping through until first access?

miriam: proposal: two-tier integrity: 1) verify manifest + signer (KMS) on load (fast), 2) defer chunk-level sha256 checks until chunk is mmap'd/read. on failure: evict chunk, re-fetch from origin and re-verify. falls back to full warmup if repeated failures.

alex: how does this interact with safetensors signed headers? we already verify header sig in index-first flows, right?

dana: yeah header signature exists. main worry is a mismatch between manifest and chunk contents if an attacker races an origin update. manifest must be signed and include content-addressed chunk ids.

miriam: exactly — manifest carries chunk ids + offsets + sizes + sha256. signature binds those. header/header-sig check stays. chunk sha256 only used for integrity & dedupe later.

praveen: eviction/refetch logic needs a sane backoff and circuit breaker so a bad disk/remote doesn't spike IO. also add telemetry: `deferred_checksum_failures`, `deferred_retries` and `deferred_stall_ms`.

miriam: agreed. also we should preserve a strict path for enterprise tenants: config `warmup.integrity_mode = {strict, deferred}` where strict forces full pre-verify/mmap at load. default deferred for best latency.

alex: do we have any perf numbers? rough sim: full warmup of a 100GB shard (read+verify) ~12s pipelined; header-verify-only + lazy chunk checks reduces initial enable to ~2s. downside: first token generation may stall if the first needed chunk hasn't finished background verify/page-in.

dana: can we stream-verify in the background at low I/O priority and use `posix_fadvise`/cgroups IO weight? that would smooth the first-token stalls.

miriam: yep — background verifier with IO niceness and a fast optimistic path: try to mmmap the first NKB w/o blocking, if page fault triggers checksum, block briefly then continue.

miriam: quick manifest example to make intent concrete: ```json
{"manifest_version":"1","model":"ggml-test","chunks":[{"id":"cid-1","offset":0,"size":67108864,"sha256":"abc123..."},{"id":"cid-2","offset":67108864,"size":67108864,"sha256":"def456..."}],"signed_by":"release-v1"}
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noted — feature-flag `deferred_checksum_verification` will be required for rollout and gradual enable. :white_check_mark:

kate: action items: miriam write RFC describing threat model + fallback behaviour; praveen outline backoff/circuit-breaker + telemetry; ops add flag + gating in console; eng-sre evaluate IO niceness options.

miriam: will do. quick naming bikeshed: `lazy_integrity` vs `deferred_checksum`. thoughts?

alex: +1 lazy_integrity (short)

praveen: +1 deferred_checksum (explicit)

dana: lazy_integrity feels ambiguous — defer to the RFC.

miriam: ok filing RFC, will ping channel with link when ready. :rocket:
